matches.quote: The electronic T_c uses a "within 15% of maximum" criterion (Fig. 4P to S). This choice is arbitrary and sets the width directly.
there is no 6L or 18L on Al2O3... the authors should: ... include a 6L/Al2O3 flake
Charge transfer and screening are inferred, not shown, and strain or interfacial chemistry has not been excluded
Measure the interfacial doping directly... Then compare the inferred carrier density with the doping levels in K-dosing (refs. 26 to 29) and gating (ref. 60) studies.
Eq. 1 has no separate background term. The 20 to 80 cm⁻¹ window also contains the Ag(o1)* leakage mode near 35 cm⁻¹ and Ag(m1) at low T.
Characterize the Ta2NiSe5/Au interface chemically... Separately, rule out lateral inhomogeneity as the source of broadening, for example from amorphous-Au roughness, partial contact or local strain.
Show quantitatively that a layer-dependent T_c profile reproduces the measured temperature dependence of Ag(m5) intensity and peak position.
The paper treats 4L/Al2O3 both as moderately perturbed and as the clean control... The authors should explain the 40 K reduction: thickness, strain, or ALD processing.
Soften "establishes an excitonic component" (p. 16) unless such discriminating evidence is added.
Perform a transfer-matrix calculation of the layer-resolved Raman weight for both stacks... Show quantitatively that a layer-dependent T_c profile reproduces the measured temperature dependence

notes: C4 asks about sensitivity of the quasi-elastic electronic Tc to the chosen 10 cm-1 wavenumber; P2 questions the arbitrary 15% threshold criterion for the same curve and P10 notes 10 cm-1 is adjacent to a removed 15 cm-1 Rayleigh leak (marked partly). C9 asks to decompose/extract the intrinsic interface-layer Raman signal, whereas P1/P6 ask to forward-model the layer-resolved Raman weights and Tc profile (marked partly). C11 notes defects in ALD Al2O3 could allow charge transfer; P7 similarly challenges treating 4L/Al2O3 as an unperturbed control given its 15% Tc reduction and ALD processing (marked partly). C12 asks to clarify the relative roles of screening and doping; P14, P15, P17, and P19 ask to measure doping directly and use spacers to separate screening length from charge transfer (marked partly).
